# pbs_apt_updates (Data Source)

Lists the package updates of a Proxmox Backup Server node, as the Updates panel of its interface shows them: every installed package whose candidate version in APT's package cache, the one an upgrade installs, differs from the installed one, and the packages those versions depend on that are not installed, which an upgrade would install anew, such as the package of a new kernel.

PBS reads APT's package cache on the node and does not refresh it: reading the data source makes no network access, and the list is as current as the node's last `apt update`. PBS's daily update runs one, and so does the **Refresh** button of the Updates panel, or the `pbs_apt_update` action. A container whose image removed APT's package lists, as images often do to save space, lists no updates until `apt update` runs in it.

Needs `Sys.Audit on /`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "pbs_apt_updates" "this" {}

# The versions of PBS's own packages an upgrade would install, such as
# { "proxmox-backup-server" = "4.2.8" }. The list is as current as the node's
# last apt update, which PBS's daily update runs.
locals {
  pbs_updates = {
    for u in data.pbs_apt_updates.this.updates : u.package => u.version
    if startswith(u.package, "proxmox-backup-")
  }
}

check "pbs_is_up_to_date" {
  assert {
    condition     = length(local.pbs_updates) == 0
    error_message = "PBS updates are available: ${jsonencode(local.pbs_updates)}."
  }
}

# Packages an upgrade would install anew, such as a new kernel.
output "new_packages" {
  value = [for u in data.pbs_apt_updates.this.updates : "${u.package} ${u.version}" if u.old_version == null]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `node` (String) Node to read: `localhost` or the node's host name. Defaults to the provider's `node`.

### Read-Only

- `updates` (Attributes List) The packages an upgrade would change or install, sorted by `package`, then `arch`; empty when the node is up to date as far as its package cache knows. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--updates))

<a id="nestedatt--updates"></a>
### Nested Schema for `updates`

Read-Only:

- `arch` (String) Architecture of the package, such as `amd64`, or `all` for one that runs on every architecture.
- `description` (String) Long description of the package, which may span several lines; empty when it has none.
- `old_version` (String) Version installed now; null for a package an upgrade would install anew.
- `origin` (String) Origin of the repository that offers `version`, such as `Proxmox` or `Debian`; `unknown` when APT does not know it.
- `package` (String) Name of the package, such as `proxmox-backup-server`.
- `priority` (String) Debian priority of the package, such as `optional` or `important`; `unknown` when APT does not know it.
- `section` (String) Debian section of the package, such as `admin` or `libs`; `unknown` when APT does not know it.
- `title` (String) Short description of the package; its name when it has none.
- `version` (String) Version an upgrade installs: the candidate version in APT's package cache.
